summary: Express 5.3.0 holds only a thin facade: lib/application.js lazily creates a `router` package Router, proxies app.use/app.handle to it, and hands `finalhandler` in as the terminal `done` callback. The actual chain (ordered Layer stack, next() continuation, error-signature routing, promise rejection catching, per-route sub-stacks) lives in the `router` dependency, a linear next() pipeline rather than an onion.

components.why: Router.handle holds the ordered `stack` of Layers and the inner next(err) loop (~line 188) that walks it, with 'route'/'router' sentinel handling and setImmediate; `use` (~404) and `route` (~425-440) push Layers onto the stack
Layer.handleRequest (~142) and handleError (~106) invoke the user function, choosing by arity, and catch sync throws plus rejected promises and forward them to next(err)
Route holds a per-route stack with its own next() loop (~119): per-method handlers form a nested chain inside the global chain
app.use (~181-235) delegates to router.use and wraps mounted sub-apps; the lazy `router` getter (~69-80) builds the Router once; app.handle (~152) is the entry
Terminal handler used as `done`: sends 404 when nothing responded, renders the error otherwise, destroys the socket if headers are already sent (~118-121)
exports the express() factory whose app is the request handler

entry_points.why: app.handle(req, res, callback) per request; builds `done` via finalhandler and calls this.router.handle
app.use registers middleware (global, path-scoped, or mounted sub-app) in registration order
the `router` function is itself a (req,res,next) middleware, so routers nest
inner next(err) is the continuation driving the chain

deps.name: router
deps.carries: the entire chain mechanics: order, next(), arity-based error handlers, async rejection capture, scope, param processing

deps.name: finalhandler
deps.carries: end-of-chain fallback: 404, error rendering, socket destroy when headers already sent

rejected.why: router.param / process_params is param pre-processing tied to route matching

notes: Express itself contains no chain code (lib/router does not exist in 5.x); verify behaviour against installed router 2.2.0. Async errors: Layer catches returned rejected promises, unlike Express 4. Body reading (D10) is not in this chain: body parsing is a separate middleware (not located). Chain built once lazily via the router getter (D9). Not verified: exact line for the double-write guard (finalhandler checks res.headersSent at ~84 and ~118).
